newsitem.title: USA: U.S. twins born 92 days apart set Guinness record.
newsitem.headline: U.S. twins born 92 days apart set Guinness record.

text.p: Twins were born a record 92 days apart after doctors delayed delivering the second baby to allow him to develop, a hospital said on Wednesday.
"We checked with the Guinness Book of World Records and confirmed it's a record," Michelle Gorham of Rockford Memorial Hospital said.

Janet Pasaye of Palatine, Illinois, gave birth to the first twin, Joshua, on Oct. 26. She was only 25 weeks into the pregnancy and Joshua weighed less than 2 pounds (0.97 kg). He remained in intensive care in the hospital on Wednesday.

On Sunday, Pasaye delivered his twin brother, Jacob, who weighed a little over 6 pounds (2.7 kg), at a suburban Chicago clinic. Doctors delayed his birth by stitching the woman's cervix closed and keeping her under hospital care for weeks.

Gorham said the record book lists 36 days between the birth of twins to an Italian woman as the current record, although doctors at the Rockford hospital have separated such births by as much as 50 days in recent years.

A few days ago a surrogate mother in Britain was reported to have given birth to a boy whose twin sister was born to a different surrogate mother 22 months earlier. The embryos were test tube conceptions.
